resolutions.researcher_notes: Original ref (saymar.org PDF) is effectively dead: URL returns 200 but no longer contains gas-pipeline content ('غاز' absent); no Wayback capture (404). Found NO source stating the project is 'shelved'. On the contrary, the live seed source (Independent Arabia, 2021-01-19) presents it as an active government project: construction approved 2019 and work 'nearing completion' as of Jan 2021 — this CONTRADICTS the 'shelved' status. Status left unresolved/dead; flag the discrepancy for the status-sweep — GEM may have been reclassified to shelved on later info I could not locate.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) states the Iraqi government approved/adopted the project in 2019 ('the Iraqi government approved construction in 2019'), supporting ProposalYear 2019. Single independent source → medium. Verified page contains '2019' and 'الرميلة الشمالية'/'النجف'/'وزارة النفط'. No second independent source found; story appears unique to Independent Arabia.

Same Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) article: government approved construction in 2019 and work was 'nearing completion' as of Jan 2021, consistent with ConstructionYear 2019. Single source → medium. Note: the article does not cleanly separate proposal vs. construction-start dates — 2019 is the approval/start year it gives.

Could not corroborate Capacity 258 MMSCMD. Original saymar.org PDF is dead; no Wayback. Independent Arabia article (verified live) does NOT contain '258' and gives only a downstream electrical figure ('more than 2,500 MW'), not a gas throughput. The '258' figure appears to trace to the related Basra–Aqaba/Iraq–Jordan project (2b1stconsulting: 350 MMSCFD within Iraq / 258 MMSCFD within Jordan, and note the unit there is MMSCFD not MMSCMD) — likely a cross-project/unit mis-derivation. Left unresolved; flag possible bad value+unit.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) explicitly: 'أنبوب يبلغ طوله أكثر من 350 كيلو متراً من حقول الرميلة الشمالية' (a pipeline more than 350 km long from the North Rumaila fields). Directly corroborates LengthKnown 350 km. Verified page contains both '350' and 'كم'. Single independent source → medium; no second source surfaced despite EN+AR searches.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) states the pipeline draws gas from the North Rumaila oil fields ('من حقول الرميلة الشمالية'), corroborating FuelSource = Rumela. Verified page contains 'الرميلة الشمالية'. Single independent source → medium.

Independent Arabia (2021-01-19) describes the line running from the North Rumaila fields (Basra governorate) to a chain of cities extending toward Najaf, corroborating Start = Rumela/Basrah, End = Al-Najaf. Verified page contains 'الرميلة الشمالية', 'البصرة', and 'النجف'. Single independent source → medium.

GEM ProposalYear=2022 is NOT corroborated and appears to CONTRADICT the independent record. All working sources place the proposal/contract in 2021: Rudaw (Arabic) says the KRG Ministry of Natural Resources signed the pipeline agreement with KAR Group in January 2021; New Lines Institute says the KDP-led KRG awarded the KAR Group contract 'in 2021'; attaqa (Aug 2022) also dates the KAR Group build contract to 2021 (other reports put the EPC appointment in December 2021). The only 2022 milestone found is PM Masrour Barzani's 8 March 2022 announcement of intent to export gas to Europe, which is not the pipeline proposal itself. Flagging for reviewer: ProposalYear likely should be 2021. Marked UNRESOLVED because no source corroborates the 2022 value.

ConstructionYear=2022 corroborated by 2+ independent sources. attaqa (Aug 2022, Arabic) reports the Khor Mor/pipeline works were active in 2022 and were suspended end-June 2022 after rocket attacks (US contractor Exterran withdrew July 2022) — i.e. construction was underway in 2022. Iraq Oil Report (Aug 2023) confirms 'Construction has begun on a 36-inch pipeline' bringing gas from the Khor Mor field toward Erbil/Dohuk. Rudaw states a 16-month implementation timeline from the Jan-2021 contract, placing active build in 2022. Independent (Arabic wire + English trade press + Kurdish outlet), tier high.

FuelSource=Khormor (Khor Mor gas field) corroborated by 2+ independent sources. NS Energy: processed gas from the Khor Mor gas facility (operated by Pearl Petroleum) is delivered to Erbil, Chemchemal and Bazian power stations. Iraq Oil Report: the new pipeline is to 'bring gas supplies from the Khor Mor field.' Tier high.

Location (Khor Mor field, Kurdistan Region of Iraq -> Erbil, Kurdistan, Iraq) corroborated by 2+ independent sources. NS Energy and Rudaw both describe the gas line running from the Khor Mor field to Erbil; New Lines describes the route from producing fields (Khor Mor/Chemchemal) to Erbil and onward to Dohuk. All place start and end in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Tier high.

Original current_ref (shafaq Khor Mor exclusive) is dead (HTTP 404); not archivable/needed since better sources exist. GEM Status = 'construction'. Rudaw Arabic (Feb 2022) reports the EPC agreement (KRG MNR with Kar Group, ~Jan 2021, 16-month build) and Iraq Oil Report notes the EPC contract was signed Dec 2021 and 'implementation has already begun' — both corroborate that the line was UNDER CONSTRUCTION through 2021-2022. IMPORTANT DISAGREEMENT: the pipeline was inaugurated by PM Masrour Barzani on 28 Oct 2025 (Shafaq, thenewregion, kurdistan24), so Status should now be updated to 'operating' — 'construction' is stale. Two independent sources for the construction-phase value.
Fuel = Gas. Every source describes this as a natural gas pipeline (Rudaw Arabic, Iraq Oil Report, Shafaq inauguration coverage). Two independent working sources; unambiguous.

PipelineType = transmission. Sources describe a ~192-198 km inter-governorate trunk line carrying gas from the Khurmala/Khor Mor fields across the Kurdistan Region (Erbil to Duhok) with spare capacity for future export destinations — clearly a transmission/trunk pipeline, not distribution. No source uses the controlled-vocab word 'transmission' literally, so tier medium (classification inferred from length/function).

GEM ProposalYear = 2022, but sources CONTRADICT this: the EPC contract was signed with Kar Group in Dec 2021 (Iraq Oil Report) and Rudaw Arabic (Feb 2022) references an agreement dated ~Jan 2021. A signed EPC contract in late 2021 means the project was proposed/agreed by 2021, not 2022. No working source corroborates a 2022 proposal date; evidence points to 2021 (or earlier). Marking UNRESOLVED and flagging the disagreement — ProposalYear likely should be 2021.

ConstructionYear = 2022. Iraq Oil Report: EPC contract signed Dec 2021 and 'implementation has already begun' (article early 2022); Rudaw Arabic (Feb 2022) cites a 16-month completion timeline from the agreement. Construction was underway in 2022 — corroborated by two independent sources. (Note: the ~Dec 2021 EPC could arguably place construction start in late 2021, but 2022 is consistent with active build.)

Diameter = 52 in. Rudaw Arabic explicitly states '52 inches' Erbil-to-Duhok; Iraq Oil Report describes 'a new 52-inch pipeline to Dohuk'. Two independent working sources agree exactly. Verifier confirmed the token '52' on both pages. High confidence.

FuelSource = 'Eribl' (typo of Erbil, the pipeline's start point). Sources confirm gas is fed from the Khurmala gas field to Erbil and onward to Duhok (Rudaw), i.e. the line originates in the Erbil area (Iraq Oil Report: 'laid from Khurmala to the power station in Duhok'). The upstream gas field is actually Khurmala (Rudaw) / Khor Mor (later 2025 coverage), so 'Erbil' reflects the pipeline start rather than the field name. Tier medium given the typo and the source-vs-start ambiguity.

Location: start Erbil, end Duhok, both in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Shafaq ('198-kilometer pipeline linking Erbil and Duhok'), Rudaw Arabic, and Kurdistan24 all confirm the Erbil->Duhok routing within Iraqi Kurdistan. Multiple independent working sources; high confidence. (Note GEM StartLocation is blank — the start is Erbil/Khurmala.)

No source explicitly corroborates GEM Status 'shelved'. MEED (24 May 2011) shows the project only ever reached the EPC bidding stage: South Oil Company tendered it in April 2011, 20+ firms submitted bids, construction was expected to take 10 months — no evidence it advanced. The Arabic ahewar survey (30 May 2022) still lists it as a planned/target project, not as shelved. So 'shelved' is a reasonable GEM inference from a stalled 2011 tender that never progressed, but it is NOT directly stated by any independent source, and the 2022 source mildly contradicts it by treating the line as still planned. Leaving proposed_refs empty to avoid an unsupported ref; flagging the disagreement for human review.

Two independent publications, different years/languages -> high.

Original current_ref (bncnetwork) dead; replaced. MEED (2011): '105-kilometre-long gas pipeline connecting the Zubair oil field to the Fao oil depot ... the Fao depot 105km away'. ahewar (2022, Arabic): 'بطول 105 كيلومتر' (length 105 km). Two independent sources agree on 105 km -> high.

Original current_ref (bncnetwork) dead; replaced. MEED (2011): '18-inch carbon steel gas pipeline'. ahewar (2022, Arabic): 'وقطر 18 بوصة' (diameter 18 inches). Two independent sources agree on 18 in -> high.

Two independent sources agree -> high.

No independent source describes this specific West Qurna->Rumaila gas pipeline as 'under construction'. Extensive EN+AR searching only surfaces the broader BGC/GGIP gas-gathering scheme (capturing associated gas from Rumaila, Zubair, West Qurna) and unrelated lines (13.7 km North Rumaila feed-gas, 80 km broadcut export, 10.2 km dry-gas grid link; a separate 40 km/42-in Khor Al-Zubair->Shatt Al-Arab dry-gas line, Iraq Business News 2025-03-16). Two independent sources, but they corroborate the gas context of the fields, not this specific named pipeline (which no source names). Tier medium for that reason.
No independent source names this pipeline, so its classification as 'transmission' cannot be corroborated. Uncorroborated.

StartYear1=2025 not corroborated by any independent source for this specific pipeline. GGIP-related gas commissioning runs 2025-2028, but no source ties a 2025 start to a West Qurna->Rumaila line. Uncorroborated.

LengthKnown=50 km not found in any independent source. Documented southern-Iraq gas lines have different lengths (13.7 km, 80 km, 10.2 km, 40 km). '50 km' appears in sources only as the distance of the Rumaila-West Qurna field west of Basra, not as a pipeline length. Uncorroborated.

Diameter=40 in not found in any independent source for this pipeline. The nearest documented figure is a separate Khor Al-Zubair->Shatt Al-Arab line at 42 in / 40 km (Iraq Business News, 2025-03-16) - different endpoints and specs, not a match. Uncorroborated.

FuelSource=Qurna corroborated: BGC explicitly lists West Qurna 1 among the fields whose associated gas it gathers/processes, and TotalEnergies GGIP includes West Qurna as a gas source. Two independent sources confirm West Qurna as a gas source in this area; they do not name this specific pipeline, hence tier medium.

Endpoints corroborated as real gas fields in southern Iraq (Basra): GeoExpro ('Rumaila-West Qurna, Iraq') and BGC both place West Qurna and Rumaila in southern Iraq. This supports StartCountryOrArea=Iraq, EndLocation=Rumela (Rumaila), EndCountryOrArea=Iraq. Two independent sources agree, so tier high for the location values. Note: neither source describes a direct pipeline between the two fields.

GEM Status=construction corroborated. wattaennews (Wattan News Agency, 2024-09-23) headline 'تقدم كبير في إعمال ربط خط أنبوب الغاز بزركان حلفاية' (significant progress in the connection works of the Bazargan-Halfaya gas pipeline), with the Maysan Oil Co. gas-dept director quoted that 'there is significant progress in the pipe-connection works, executed by a contractor to which the project was assigned.' Wayback-archived iraq-businessnews (2025-03-18, sourcing INA) states '80% progress has been made on a 60-kilometer gas pipeline linking Buzurgan to Halfaya.' Also independently supported by al-mirbad (2023-05-26): implementing company had begun site handover, topographic and pipeline-route survey. Two+ independent reports at different dates -> under construction. tier high. (Original current_ref iraq-businessnews 2024 article now returns HTTP 401 behind a bot-wall -> not stageable; its Wayback copy verifies but I staged fresher/independent corroboration.)

Fuel=Gas confirmed. Every source describes a gas pipeline: wattaennews 'خط أنبوب الغاز بزركان حلفاية' (Bazargan-Halfaya gas pipeline), Wayback iraq-businessnews 2024 'the 18-inch gas pipeline between Bazargan and Halfaya.' Two independent working sources. tier high.

PipelineType=transmission corroborated. al-mirbad (2023) explicitly 'مد الأنبوب الناقل من البزركان إلى حقل الحلفاية' (laying the transmission/carrier pipe from Bazargan to Halfaya field); wattaennews describes it as part of 'خطوط الأنابيب النفطية التابعة لوزارة النفط' (the Oil Pipelines Company network under the Ministry of Oil) carrying field gas ~70 km to power plants. A field-to-power-plant transmission line, not a distribution/gathering line. Two independent sources. tier high.

Capacity=70 MMcf/d corroborated. wattaennews (2024): Maysan Oil Co. supplies surplus gas 'بكمية تترواح من (٦٠ إلى ٧٠) مقمق' (60-70 MMscf/d). Wayback iraq-businessnews (2025, sourcing INA): 'gas compression unit with a processing capacity of up to 70 million standard cubic feet per day (MMscf)' and elsewhere 'a gas compression unit with a processing capacity of 50-70 MMscf.' GEM's 70 sits at the top of the reported range; both sources agree on 70 as the figure. Two independent reports months apart. tier high (minor note: sources give a 50/60-70 range, GEM uses the 70 ceiling).

Diameter=18 in corroborated by one source: Wayback-archived iraq-businessnews (2024-07-24), quoting Deputy Minister of Oil for Gas Affairs Ezzat Saber on 'the 18-inch gas pipeline between Bazargan and Halfaya' (Source: Ministry of Oil). Only one origin found (the Ministry-of-Oil statement, republished by iraq-businessnews; live page 401s so the verified Wayback copy is staged). Arabic searches for a diameter (قطر ١٨ بوصة/انج) did not surface an independent second source. tier medium, single origin.

FuelSource=Bazargan Field corroborated. Both sources: a gas compressor unit (GCU) is installed 'في حقل البزركان' (in the Bazargan field) to capture associated gas produced there, which is then piped to Halfaya. wattaennews and al-mirbad are independent (2024 vs 2023). tier high.

Location Bazargan -> Halfaya (Maysan, Iraq) corroborated. al-mirbad (Maysan Oil Co. statement): 'مد الأنبوب الناقل من البزركان إلى حقل الحلفاية' (pipe from Bazargan to Halfaya field), in Maysan governorate. wattaennews: Bazargan-Halfaya line within Maysan Oil Company fields. Wayback iraq-businessnews also 'between Bazargan and Halfaya,' tagged Maysan/Missan. Both fields are in Maysan (Missan) province, Iraq. Two+ independent sources. tier high.

The flagged DEAD_LINK current_ref (al-mirbad/157543, dated 2 May 2024) re-verified live (verifier 200 + content present) — the failure was transient. It reports active advanced-stage construction ('العمل مستمر للمشروع وبمراحل متقدمة كنصب المعدات وإكمال الأعمال الميكانيكية'), consistent with Status='construction'. Independently corroborated: attaqa.net (Dec 2025) describes the project as still in an advanced execution phase progressing rapidly with initial operation targeted for Q1 2027; Egypt Oil & Gas (English) says the project 'nears operational phase' with equipment delivered and installation set to begin, not yet operational. Three independent outlets all place the project mid-construction (not operational), so Status='construction' is well supported. High.

No independent source corroborates ConstructionYear=2024 as the year construction STARTED; the evidence points earlier and CONTRADICTS 2024 as a start year. Baker Hughes/BHGE won the SGC contract in Aug 2018; per S&P Global / Oil&Gas Middle East reporting, agreements were signed 2021 and construction started ~2022. al-mirbad/132346 (dated 20 Feb 2023) reports the project already 47% complete, and al-mirbad/157476 & /157543 (May 2024) show equipment/civil installation still ongoing in 2024. So 2024 at best reflects construction still in progress, not its start. The single staged ref (al-mirbad/157543) documents active pipeline/equipment construction during 2024 but does not corroborate '2024' as a start year (contains_value=false). RECOMMEND: review ConstructionYear — construction start is better characterized as ~2022. Left UNRESOLVED for the value as stated.

GEM Status = construction. The original current_ref (iraqieconomists.net PDF) returns HTTP 200 but the document does NOT mention this pipeline (verifier fails on 'Rumaila'; WebFetch confirms no Faiha/North-Rumaila pipeline content) — so it is not a usable source for this row and is dropped. New corroboration: (1) attaqa.net (Iraqi energy outlet 'منصة الطاقة', 7 Apr 2026) reports Oil Projects Company (شركة المشاريع النفطية) BEGAN implementing a new gas pipeline pushing gas toward the North Rumaila liquids-separation (NGL) plant via the compressor site near Yamama station (محطة اليمامة, a Faiha-field reservoir): 20-inch dia, 55 mmcf/d, Phase-1 hot-tapping tie-in + Phase-2 3 km extension, target 15-day completion — i.e. actively under construction. (2) al-mirbad.com (8 May 2025) explicitly names 'مشروع الفيحاء' (the Faiha project) gas lines being commissioned/inaugurated ('تدشين خطي غاز') mid-May 2025. Tier MEDIUM not high: only attaqa is substantive, and it corroborates construction toward North Rumaila but does not literally name 'Faiha'; al-mirbad names Faiha but is a thin video-snippet page and a separate/earlier event. TIMING FLAG for review: al-mirbad's May-2025 'inauguration' vs attaqa's Apr-2026 'just-started new line' suggest GEM's single row may bundle multiple phases — status could be past pure 'construction' for the earlier line. NOTE: the sotaliraq.com (14 Apr 2026) piece feeding the same North Rumaila NGL plant is a DIFFERENT project (Bin Umar / أبن عمر gas investment), deliberately NOT used to avoid conflating two pipelines.

GEM Location: Start = Basrah, Iraq; End = North Rumaila oil field, Basrah, Iraq. attaqa.net (7 Apr 2026) confirms the pipeline pushes gas toward 'معمل فصل السوائل في الرميلة الشمالية' (the North Rumaila liquids-separation/NGL plant) via the compressor site near 'محطة اليمامة' (Yamama station) — all in Basra governorate — strongly corroborating the North-Rumaila / Basrah END and Basrah location. The Faiha START is supported by (a) al-mirbad (8 May 2025) naming the 'Faiha project' (الفيحاء) gas lines and (b) the Yamama-station link, since Yamama is one of the Faiha field's reservoirs (Al-Yamama/Mishrif/Al-Zubair per baghdadtoday/zagrosnews coverage of the July-2024 Faiha CPF opening). Tier MEDIUM: the North Rumaila/Basrah end is well corroborated by attaqa; the Faiha start rests on the Yamama-field inference plus al-mirbad rather than an explicit 'Faiha → North Rumaila' statement in one source. No contradiction with GEM values.

'Okaz' = عكاز = Akkas gas field in Al-Anbar province, western Iraq; the pipeline connects the field to the (still-under-construction) Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant. GEM Status = 'proposed' is well corroborated: the pipeline is not yet built. Per the July 22 2025 Schlumberger/Midland Oil field-development contract, a PARALLEL contract (with SCOP, the State Company for Oil Projects) is to be signed to build a pipeline network linking wells to central processing units, with gas then directed to the Anbar power plant. The National: 'Additional contracts will be signed to build surface installations and lay pipelines connecting the wells to central processing units' (verified). Iraqi News: names the SCOP pipeline-network contract and the 100 mmscfd/Anbar power-plant destination (verified, contains Akkas+Anbar+SCOP). Xinhua: confirms the newly-signed deal to develop the field with output routed to the Anbar power plant (verified). Field currently produces only ~40 mmscfd; the transmission pipeline is planned/to-be-built = proposed. Caveat on independence: all three outlets report the same July 2025 Ministry-of-Oil announcement, but each carries distinct detail (The National's 'long-awaited'/pipeline-to-CPU line vs Iraqi News's SCOP-network specifics), and none cite GEM. Tier high on the value (proposed/planned pipeline). The original current_ref (iraqieconomists.net PDF, Al-Jibawi) returns HTTP 200 but the url_verifier could not extract the 'Okaz'/'Anbar' tokens from it (appears to be a scanned/non-text-extractable PDF), so it is not staged; the three fresh news sources supersede it.

Unit was DEAD_LINK: the only citation (iraqieconomists.net Al-Jibawi PDF) is live (HTTP 200) but on WebFetch its text does NOT mention Akkas/Okaz, Anbar pipelines, or a T1-K3 segment at all — it is a misattributed citation, so it cannot support the Status. Kept as ok=false/contains_value=false. GEM entity = a PROPOSED 3-segment gas trunk from the Okaz (Akkas) field via stations T1 and K3 to Al-Anbar (T1-K3 = 26in, owner Iraqi Ministry of Oil); this is the wider gas-TRANSPORT network, distinct from the short ~30km line that already feeds the adjacent Akkas power station. Corroborated 'proposed' with two independent professional outlets: (1) The National (2025-07-22) — 'Additional contracts will be signed to build surface installations and lay pipelines connecting the wells to central processing units,' gas then directed to the Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant (still under construction) = pipeline network planned, not built, owner Iraqi Ministry of Oil. (2) MEES (2025-07-25) — states current output (~40mn cfd) runs via an existing 30km line to the Akkas power plant, while SCOP will ADD new flow lines from SLB-drilled wells to new processing units under a forthcoming contract = the expanded transport pipelines are planned. Both distinguish the built local feed from the still-to-be-built transport network, matching Status=proposed. Tier high: two reputable independent outlets each with their own operational reporting; caveat — both cover the same July 2025 SLB/Akkas award, though the qualitative 'planned pipeline network' status is also consistent with earlier (2022) MEES and Iraq Oil Report coverage. iraq-businessnews.com/2025/07/22 aggregator returned HTTP 401 (not usable).
